title: Find duplicate trade IDs in second-occurrence order
description: A trade feed may repeat a record. Return each duplicated ID once, ordered by when its second occurrence arrives.
contract: Input: one comma-separated list. A dash (-) means an empty list; ~ means a null list or ID. Output: comma-separated duplicates, or -. Reject a null list, null ID or blank ID with ERROR. Do not trim or normalise valid IDs.
constraints: Use Java 17 and the standard library. Do not add a package declaration.
For this terminal interface, identifiers contain no commas, pipes, equals signs or line breaks. Match identifiers exactly and case-sensitively.
Use the supplied Main entry point. Print only the required result; diagnostics belong on standard error.

explanation: Validate IDs before recording them so incomplete records cannot become map keys.
The map stores the number of times an ID has appeared. Append an ID only when its new count is exactly two; later retries do not append it again.
Walking the feed in encounter order makes the second occurrence determine the output position. For n IDs and u distinct IDs, expected time is O(n) and additional storage is O(u).
A production feed needs a retention window and a policy for conflicting payloads, which this ID-only exercise deliberately leaves to the follow-up.

title: Build an idempotent ledger posting service
description: Implement an in-memory ledger that applies each posting once, rejects conflicting retries and preserves exact balances.
contract: Input: postingId,accountId,amount records, or -. Amounts are signed decimal values with at most two fractional digits; zero is allowed. Output: alphabetical account=balance pairs with exactly two decimals. A consistent retry contributes once. Reusing an ID with a different account or numeric amount produces ERROR. Negative account balances are permitted in this simplified ledger; no overdraft rule is implied.
constraints: Use Java 17 and the standard library. Do not add a package declaration.
For this terminal interface, identifiers contain no commas, pipes, equals signs or line breaks. Match identifiers exactly and case-sensitively.
Use the supplied Main entry point. Print only the required result; diagnostics belong on standard error.
Inputs contain at most 10,000 records unless a narrower limit is stated. Output must be at most 64 KiB.

title: Make execution counting thread-safe
description: Multiple workers replay execution IDs concurrently. Count each distinct ID exactly once, even when retries race.
contract: Input: workers|replays|comma-separated event IDs. workers is 1–8; replays 1–100; at most 1,000 IDs; - means no IDs. The supplied adapter submits every ID on every replay to an ExecutorService. Output: the number of distinct exact IDs after all work finishes. Implement Counter.accept and Counter.size. Automated results check observed outcomes; they do not prove race freedom under every schedule.

ConcurrentHashMap.newKeySet supplies a thread-safe set whose add operation is atomic. A separate contains followed by add on an ordinary HashSet is unsafe.
Wait for every submitted Future before inspecting the final size. Otherwise the snapshot may be observed before processing completes.
Stress cases can reveal races but cannot prove their absence. Explain the collection contract and the happens-before relationship established by Future.get.

title: Build a bounded regression task runner
description: Execute independent regression tasks with a bounded pool, preserve submission order and isolate individual task failures.
contract: Input: workers on line 1 (1–8), then taskId,value records. value is an integer or FAIL. Output: taskId=value or taskId=ERROR in submission order; - when no tasks exist. Runner.execute receives Callable<String> tasks and must use a bounded ExecutorService, await every result, isolate failed tasks and shut down resources. Output tests check ordering/failure handling; bounded execution and cleanup require code review.

Read Futures in submission order to preserve output order, even when tasks finish in another order.
Catch ExecutionException per task, so one failure becomes one ERROR result while remaining tasks are still observed.
Restore interruption when handling InterruptedException and always shut down the executor in finally. Review lifecycle and concurrency separately from functional output.
